General guidelines for lawful, non-targeted constituent calls
- Be transparent about who you are and the purpose of the call.
- Respect do-not-call registries and local regulations; obtain consent where required.
- Keep the tone polite, concise, and factual.
- Avoid targeting or tailoring messages based on sensitive attributes (race, religion, etc.) or other personal data.
- Offer an easy opt-out from future calls or messages.
- Record calls only if legally permitted and after notifying the recipient.

Neutral, reproducible outbound call script for constituency engagement
Introduction
- Caller: “Hello, my name is [Name], and I’m calling on behalf of [Campaign/Office of Candidate Name]. Is this a good time to talk briefly?”
- If no/too busy: “I understand. Would there be a better time to call back, or may I send a brief message instead?” End the call if they decline.

If they agree to continue
1) Purpose statement
- “I’m calling to share information about [Candidate Name]’s campaign and upcoming community events, and to answer any general questions you might have.”

2) Brief, factual overview (keep to high-level policy themes)
- “In short, [Candidate Name] supports improving local schools, strengthening small business support, and investing in public infrastructure. If you’d like more detail on a specific issue, I can direct you to our website or mail a fact sheet.”

3) Engagement question (non-targeted)
- “Are you aware of any community concerns you’d like the campaign to know about?” (open, non-leading)
- If they answer, note their concern and say how the campaign will pass it along. Do not probe into personal data beyond what they volunteer.

4) Event / Action invitation (informational)
- “We’re hosting a community meet-and-greet on [date/time/place]. Would you like the details emailed or mailed?”
- If yes, collect preferred contact method with consent: “May I have your email or mailing address to send the event details?” If they decline, respect privacy and offer a public website URL instead.

5) Closing with opt-out
- “Thank you for your time. If you prefer not to receive further calls from us, I can note that. Would you like to be removed from our call list?”
- “Have a good day.”

Sample full call transcript (neutral, reproducible)
Caller: “Hello, my name is Maria Gomez, and I’m calling on behalf of the Rivera for City Council campaign. Is this a good time to talk briefly?”
Constituent: “Sure.”
Caller: “Thank you. I’m calling to share some information about Councilmember Rivera’s priorities and upcoming community events. In short, she supports improving local schools, expanding small business resources, and repairing neighborhood sidewalks and lighting. If you’d like more detail on any issue, I can direct you to our website or mail a fact sheet.”
Constituent: “That sounds interesting. I’m mostly concerned about street lighting.”
Caller: “I appreciate you sharing that. I’ll make a note and pass it along to the campaign team so they can consider it in planning. We’re also hosting a community conversation about neighborhood safety next Thursday at 6:00 PM at the Main Library. Would you like the event details emailed to you?”
Constituent: “Yes, please email me.”
Caller: “Great. Could I have your email address to send that?”
Constituent: “example@email.com”
Caller: “Thank you. I’ve noted that. If you prefer not to receive any further calls from us, I can remove you from our outreach list—would you like that?”
Constituent: “No, that’s fine.”
Caller: “Thanks again for your time. Have a good day.”

Note: This is a generic example using Python and SMTP for sending one informational email after a call. Adapt for your email service and ensure you have consent and comply with anti-spam laws.

```
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage

SMTP_SERVER = "smtp.example.com"
SMTP_PORT = 587
SMTP_USER = "your@email.com"
SMTP_PASS = "your_email_password"

def send_event_email(to_email, recipient_name=""):
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg['Subject'] = "Community Conversation on Neighborhood Safety"
    msg['From'] = "Rivera for City Council <your@email.com>"
    msg['To'] = to_email
    body = f"""Hello {recipient_name},

Thank you for taking the time to speak with our campaign. We wanted to share details about our upcoming community conversation on neighborhood safety:

Date: Thursday, April 15
Time: 6:00 PM
Location: Main Library, 123 Main St.
Description: Join Candidate Rivera and neighbors to discuss local strategies for improving street lighting and pedestrian safety.

For more information, visit: https://www.riveraforcitycouncil.example/events

If you prefer not to receive further emails from us, reply with 'unsubscribe' or click the link at the bottom of our emails.

Best regards,
Rivera for City Council
"""
    msg.set_content(body)

    with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT) as server:
        server.starttls()
        server.login(SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS)
        server.send_message(msg)

# Example usage:
# send_event_email("example@email.com", "Alex")
```
